spec.research_notes:
WHAT I READ: the approved model (death-safe-points.json judged.recommended), the README decisions, the final approved text, the private design reference (sections 4, 7, 8 and the game cards), the Look 2 style test and character sheets, and the current code. In the code: _fail_beat at main.gd:1706 gives about 1.45 s to control (hit-stop 0.06, controls off 0.7, fade 0.4, fade-in 0.35). GAMEPLAY_ZOOM is 1.35. GAMEPLAY_CAMERA_Y is 360 on desktop and 392 on touch, and FLOOR_Y is 440. So the floor sits at canvas y 378 on desktop and 335 on touch, and a standing engineer's head (70 world px tall at D=4) is at about y 283 and 240. Touch buttons: Use at (773,345)-(928,435) and Pause at (854,16)-(942,72). The BottomBar dialogue panel is at 444-526. Stretch mode is canvas_items with the default keep aspect, so phones are pillarboxed. Reduced Motion today means no shake, no hit-stop and shorter flashes.

TIMING CONFLICT, RESOLVED: judged.recommended says the card accepts input after 2.4 s (0.8 s on a repeat death). The later README decision says the card is skippable back to control in about 1.5 s. The README wins. All three looks accept RETRY at 0.90 s after the hit, take 0.25 s to fade out, restore, and fade in over 0.35 s, so a player who presses at once has control at about 1.50 s. That matches today's knockdown (1.45 s) and sits between Celeste's roughly 2.0 s and roughly 1.1 s skipped (both from the private reference). The card never auto-advances, and Pause and Back stay live.

WHAT MAKES A DEATH BEAT LAND WITHOUT FRUSTRATION (findings):
1. Speed of return is the main frustration lever. Hotline Miami's instant restart is called "the single most important aspect", and reviewers add that long reloads would make it "unplayably frustrating". Celeste's "lightning fast respawn" with a checkpoint per room keeps a punishing game "pleasant". Reviewers said Little Nightmares' reload after death was "just the wrong side of being too long" and its checkpoints sat far back; Little Nightmares II fixed this with per-room checkpoints. Alien: Isolation reviewers say losing progress to a death you could not see coming "isn't scary, just frustrating". Rule: a short, skippable beat, then a near retry.
2. Sound continuity sells "no time passed". INSIDE fades to black and resets while the score plays on uninterrupted. Andersen on Limbo: "even if you die and respawn, the music will continue playing underneath". The reference targets a 0 ms audio gap. Rule: duck and filter the room tone, never cut it, and let the ringing tone ride over it.
3. Name the cause in one plain line, and keep it visible. Katana Zero freezes and rewinds with a line saying the attempt won't work, so each death becomes "a tactical data point rather than a dead end". Dark Souls and Sekiro show one huge word ("YOU DIED", the 死 kanji). That is iconic, but it shows no cause, and Dark Souls' slow fade-in is the theatrical opposite of our 1.5 s budget. Rule: a sentence about the cause, set small and calm, never a shout word, never typed out letter by letter (that reads as a terminal).
4. The screen shows aftermath, not gore. A Plague Tale "snaps to black" at its worst moment and lets the black do the work. Hollow Knight fades back in from black at the bench. Signalis marks death by the light leaving Elster's eye. Rule: drain, darken or frame, and let the image go quiet.
5. Companion staging must never read as rescue. BioShock Infinite's Elizabeth revive was criticised as "magical balancing" that removed threat. Yorda as a game-over condition is already in the reference's warnings. Rule: WOLF's reaction is a presentation-only gesture that starts after the collapse, sits on its own line, and is never followed by anything that looks like him causing the retry.
6. Subjective sound: a ringing tone plus muffled room sound is an established film device for trauma ("The Tinnitus Trope", Cine-Files). Saving Private Ryan codified it and Children of Men uses it after the café bomb. Game Accessibility Guidelines say an important sound needs a caption or visual, so CAPTION_RINGING shows for the whole sequence, even when audio is muted.
7. Text on the image: Xbox XAG 101 body minimums are 18 px at 1080p (PC) and 26 px (console). Our 16 canvas px floor is 21.3 px at 720p and 32 px at 1080p, which clears both. Lines stay at 80 characters or fewer. Text goes on calm image regions (wall above the actors, floor below) or on the void, with a soft radial scrim instead of a bordered box, because a box with a cyan accent bar is the game's existing UI-panel and terminal language.
8. Phones: Apple HIG asks for 44x44 pt minimum targets and no essential content under the sensor housing or home indicator. The reference notes INSIDE on iOS was "so dark that I can't tell whether there is something to interact with". Pillarboxing (76 pt per side on an iPhone 15) already clears the 59 pt sensor inset. The binding phone margin is the bottom (21 pt, about 29 canvas px), so every text bottom stays at or above canvas y 508.
9. Photosensitivity: WCAG 2.3.1 sets no more than three flashes per second. Best practice is to avoid flashing entirely and use tints and freeze frames instead. Rule: zero flashes in the death sequence, one-direction luminance ramps of at least 0.25 s, no flicker or glitch effects.

MOCKS (rendered stills, not played): layout mocks are in [session scratch, not kept]/death-screen/mocks/. Files: look-{a,b,c}-{disclose,press}-1280.png, look-{a,b,c}-phone.png (iPhone 15 landscape at 2x with the touch layout and safe-area guides) and contact-sheet.png. The generator is death-screen/tools/mock.py. It uses the game's Montserrat and Roboto variable TTFs (copied into tools/), the Look 2 plate and characters, the real camera framing, and the sentry card with the dropped line, for Rowan. The collapse pose in the mocks is a placeholder (the idle cut-out laid on its side). A real Look 2 collapse pose is a new asset. I measured worst-case widths in canvas px. The sentry card is 604 px at 26 px with Rowan, 667 px with an 11-letter name, and 800 px with 12 W's. DEATH_CASE_DROPPED is 572 px at 18 px. The caption is 353 px at 16 px. Everything fits one line for names up to about 11 characters, so the rule is autowrap with at most 2 lines. Nothing here has been built, played or device-tested.

SOURCES (web): https://www.pcgamer.com/katana-zero-review ; https://indiegamereviewer.com/katana-zero-review-vying-for-greatness/ ; https://stevivor.com/reviews/hotline-miami/ ; https://gameluster.com/celeste-magically-grueling-rollercoaster-emotion-fun/ ; https://hypercritic.org/collection/extremely-ok-games-celeste-2018-review ; https://teentix.org/blog/death-is-not-game-over-in-playdeads-inside ; https://www.thesixthaxis.com/?p=286764 (Little Nightmares) ; https://waytoomany.games/2021/02/18/review-little-nightmares-ii ; https://Gamespot.com/reviews/alien-isolation-review/1900-6415897/ ; https://www.pushsquare.com/reviews/ps4/alien_isolation ; https://knowyourmeme.com/memes/you-died ; https://www.avclub.com/sekiro-shadows-die-twice-death ; https://remapradio.com/articles/the-decisions-behind-a-plague-tales-most-painful-choice/ ; https://hollowknight.wiki/w/Knight ; https://signalis.wiki.gg/wiki/Endings ; https://bit-tech.net/reviews/gaming/pc/bioshock-infinite-10-things-it-got-wrong/2/ ; https://www.thecine-files.com/the-tinnitus-trope/ ; https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Shell-Shock_Silence ; https://gameaccessibilityguidelines.com/provide-captions-or-visuals-for-significant-background-sounds/ ; https://devdocs.xbox.com/build/game-principles/accessibility/xag-deep-dives/xag-101-text-display.md ; https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/three-flashes.html ; https://developer-rno.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/foundations/layout ; https://www.supercheats.com/red-dead-redemption-2/walkthrough/what-happens-when-you-die . Private: docs/research-2026-10/design-reference-25-games.md sections 4, 7, 8 and 11 (INSIDE, Limbo, Celeste timings, Hollow Knight Shade, Alien, phone darkness).

looks.name: A. Cold Still
looks.idea: At the moment the engineer lands, the world stops: hazards, steam, sparks and the sentry freeze on that frame and drain to cold grey. WOLF and the engineer are the only things not frozen. So the player sees what got them, held still like evidence, and WOLF's choice is the only motion on screen. A quiet card sits on the empty wall above them. Fits the evidence theme: the death becomes a still you can read.
looks.sequence:
t is seconds after the lethal contact.
0.00: commit first (save written, unsecured entries become DROPPED, an earlier drop becomes LOST), then visuals. Gameplay actions are released and the input buffer is cleared. The cause sound starts (blast boom, sentry servo clank, coolant frost crackle). Hit-stop 0.06 s. No white flash; the knockdown's flash call is not used on a death.
0.00-0.15: all buses duck to -30 dB behind a 500 Hz low-pass. The ringing tone fades in.
0.10: the caption chip fades in (0.15 s).
0.00-0.45: the engineer collapses. Knees 0.18 s, then slumps onto their side 0.27 s. Grim, not gory: no blood, no impact effect on the body.
0.45: world freeze. Room hazards, particles and the sentry pause on their current frame; the actors and UI keep running. If the frame holds a blast fireball, it freezes on the first post-peak frame, and drained brightness is capped at L* 70.
0.30-1.20: drain, one direction with ease-out. World saturation goes 1.0 to 0.08, brightness x0.62, with a cold multiply. Actors drain only to 0.30 saturation and x0.80, so the engineer and WOLF stay distinguishable.
0.60-0.90: the card fades in (alpha only, no slide): rule, then the cause line. The dropped line, if any, follows at 0.75.
0.90: the RETRY prompt fades in (0.15 s) and input is accepted. Only a fresh press counts; a held button from gameplay does not.
0.50-2.40: WOLF's reaction plays. His narrator line fades onto the card at 1.40.
SKIP PATH: RETRY at 0.90, then 0.25 s fade to void #000307, then restore at 1.15 (dropped case placed, junction re-synced), then 0.35 s fade-in. Control at about 1.50 s.
UNSKIPPED: settled by about 2.4 s. The card holds and never auto-advances. The ringing eases 6 dB lower by 4 s and holds faintly. Pause and Back work.
REPEAT DEATH IN THE SAME BEAT: card at 0.35 s, input at 0.60 s, WOLF goes straight to his end pose. Control at about 1.2 s if skipped; settled by about 2 s.
looks.layout:
Units are 960x540 canvas px. Values at 1280x720 are x4/3 and shown in brackets. Hidden while the card is up: TopBar HUD, BottomBar/Story, ContextHint panel, TutorialPrompt. Pause stays live.

- Caption chip: top-left at x 32, y 28 [43, 37]. Montserrat SemiBold 600, 16 px [21], caps, tracking 0.12 em. Colour #c3c5d7 on rgba(7,16,26,0.84), radius 6, padding 12x7. A static three-bar tone glyph sits before the text; it is never animated. Chip width about 393 px [524].
- Card: a centred column, x 80-880, max width 800 [107-1173, 1067]. Behind it, a soft radial scrim: an ellipse 800x200 centred at (480,150), #000307 fading from 66% to 0. No border and no accent bar, so it does not read as a UI panel or terminal.
- Rule: 60x1.5 px, #82c3e6 at 60%, centred, y 98 [131].
- Cause line: Roboto Medium 500, 26 px [35], #e3f6fe, centred, vertical centre y 124 [165].
- DEATH_CASE_DROPPED: Roboto 400, 18 px [24], #ade4fb, centre y 162 [216]. It has the case-with-a-gap icon (21 px outline case, right wall open) 10 px left of the text, so it reads as both text and shape.
- CASE_LOST_NOTICE, when present: replaces the dropped line at y 162. When both apply, LOST goes at y 186 and the WOLF line moves to 216.
- WOLF line: Roboto 400, 18 px [24], #82c3e6, centre y 194 [259].
- The block must end above y 215; the standing head line is at about 283.
- RETRY: centred at y 478 [637]. A 28x28 [37] keycap outline in #82c3e6 shows the bound glyph from settings_menu.prompt(&"interact", is_pad). Then a 13 px gap, then RETRY in Montserrat 650, 18 px [24], tracking 0.12, #e3f6fe. It reads 'E  RETRY' or 'A  RETRY'.
- Wrap: the cause line autowraps at 800 px, with at most 2 lines. On 2 lines the whole stack moves up 18 px.
- If the engineer's screen top is above y 250 (future height changes), the block moves to the floor zone, centred on y 400-460.

PHONE (landscape; iPhone 15 is 852x393 pt; the canvas is pillarboxed to 699x393 pt, so 1 canvas px = 0.728 pt):
- Phone type set: cause 30 px (21.8 pt), secondary lines 21 px (15.3 pt), caption 18 px (13.1 pt), prompt 20 px (14.6 pt).
- The touch camera puts the floor at y 335, so the card stack sits at y 92 (rule), 120, 160 and 194 and ends at y 212 or above.
- Caption chip at (24,24). Pause (854,16)-(942,72) stays.
- The Left and Right buttons hide. The Use button (773,345)-(928,435), which is 113x66 pt, relabels to RETRY (approved touch_use text).
- 'TAP RETRY' sits in the prompt slot: centred, y 478, Montserrat 650, 20 px. Tap-anywhere is off, so panic taps cannot skip the card.
- Margins: at least 24 canvas px at the sides and top. Every text bottom is at y 508 or above (home indicator 21 pt, about 29 px).
- The pillarbox (76 pt per side) clears the 59 pt sensor inset.
- At 30 px the cause wraps at 860 px; with 2 lines it drops to 26 px.
Mocks: look-a-disclose-1280.png, look-a-press-1280.png, look-a-phone.png.
looks.wolf:
Both reactions start at about 0.5 s, after the collapse has read, so neither can look like a save. He never touches, nudges, carries or fetches. The pose holds until RETRY, and after the retry he is wherever his restore point puts him.

DISCLOSE ('WOLF comes in fast and does not leave.'): within 0.2 s he turns his head (wolf-side-lookback). He crosses the frozen grey room at about 350 px/s (1.6x FOLLOW_SPEED) and stops 40-48 px from the engineer, on the side away from the hazard. He never stands in the blast span, the cloud or the sentry's path. Then he lies down beside them (a new pose; wolf-sit is the stand-in), head low and eye on the engineer. Seen against the frozen world, he is the one thing that chose to move.

PRESS ('WOLF holds his distance and looks away.'): he stops where he is, or settles at 150 px or more. His body faces the engineer and his head turns away (wolf-side-lookback mirrored so the body points at the engineer). He holds still, stays in the room and stays in frame.

Off-screen at death: the approved edge marker shows on his side and the line still appears; he does not need to arrive.

Repeat deaths: he goes straight to the end pose. The capped respawn lines (WOLF_RESPAWN_*) play after the retry as approved, not on the card.
looks.audio:
Cause sting on contact: the blast boom is cut at 80 ms; the sentry gets a servo clank; the coolant gets a frost crackle. Then all buses duck -30 dB in 0.15 s behind a 500 Hz low-pass, so the room tone becomes a muffled bed. It is never cut.

The engineer gives one exhale. No scream, no impact gore sound.

The ringing tone is procedural and hearing-safe. It is a 2.6 kHz sine with a 5.2 kHz partial at -18 dB and a slow 0.25 Hz drift of plus or minus 1.5 dB. It is capped at -24 dBFS on its own bus under Master, and it eases 6 dB lower by 4 s. Because the world is frozen, frozen hazards also stop making sound (the sentry servo and steam fall silent); only the filtered room tone remains, so the stillness is heard too.

CAPTION_RINGING shows from 0.10 s until the retry fade ends, and it shows even when the mixer is muted.

On RETRY: the tone fades over 0.6 s, the low-pass opens over 0.4 s, and the restored room's tone runs underneath with a 0 ms gap.
looks.reduced_motion:
No hit-stop, no shake. The collapse is a cut to the down pose (approved). WOLF still walks to his spot, as character animation with no camera movement. The world freeze is kept, since it removes motion rather than adding it. The drain is kept, as a single monotonic colour ramp.

Photosensitivity (applies with or without Reduced Motion): zero flashes in the sequence. Every luminance change is one direction and takes at least 0.25 s. The frozen frame is capped at L* 70, so a held fireball is never a bright still. Nothing blinks; the prompt fades in once.

The card, the caption and the timing are identical with Reduced Motion on.
references: Katana Zero: the failure freezes and rewinds with a line saying the attempt won't work, so a death becomes 'a tactical data point' (PC Gamer; Indie Game Reviewer)
Celeste: about 2.0 s death-to-control, about 1.1 s skipped (private reference); 'lightning fast respawn' (GameLuster)
Hotline Miami: instant restart as the core anti-frustration device (Stevivor)
INSIDE / Limbo: audio continues through the respawn (TeenTix; Andersen via the private reference)
Children of Men / Saving Private Ryan: the ringing-tone point-of-audition trope (The Cine-Files)
Game Accessibility Guidelines: caption significant background sounds; WCAG 2.3.1: three flashes

looks.name: B. Last Light
looks.idea: The room does not stop; it goes out. Over about 1.4 s the world fades almost to black until three lights are left. WOLF's cyan seam light, the engineer's thin rim silhouette, and a dim, steady ember from the thing that killed them (the sentry's red eye, the door seam's amber, the cloud's frost). WOLF's choice is told in light. If he comes in, his glow covers the engineer. If he holds back, his light stays on his own body and the engineer has only the faint rim.
looks.sequence:
0.00: commit, then the cause sting and hit-stop 0.06 s. No flash.
0.00-0.15: duck to -30 dB behind a low-pass. The ringing tone fades in.
0.10: the caption chip fades in.
0.00-0.45: collapse, as in Look A.
0.20-1.60: the light mask lowers world exposure to 4%, one direction with ease-in-out. The hazards keep running in the dark but are not lit.
- The cause ember fades from the hazard's own light to a steady 25%. It never flickers.
- WOLF's light is a radial additive cyan, #4f8ab8 core to #82c3e6 edge, radius about 70 world px.
- The engineer keeps a minimum rim of #4175a0 at 60% opacity, so they are always findable.
0.70-1.05: the card fades in directly on the black, with no scrim. The dropped line follows at 0.85.
0.90: RETRY appears and input is accepted.
0.50-2.20: WOLF's reaction plays. His line fades in at 1.40.
SKIP PATH: RETRY at 0.90, then 0.20 s to full void, then restore at 1.10, then 0.40 s fade-in in which the room lights come up first and the actors follow. Control at about 1.50 s.
UNSKIPPED: settled by about 2.2 s. The card holds and never auto-advances.
REPEAT DEATH: fade-down shortened to 0.6 s, card at 0.40 s, input at 0.60 s.
looks.layout:
Same chrome and type as Look A, but on void with no scrim.

- Card column x 80-880 [107-1173]. Cause line Roboto 500, 26 px [35], #e3f6fe, centre y 132 [176]. Dropped line Roboto 400, 18 px [24], #ade4fb with the case-gap icon, centre y 170 [227]. WOLF line Roboto 400, 18 px [24], #82c3e6, centre y 202 [269].

PHONE (landscape, pillarboxed, 1 canvas px = 0.728 pt):
- Phone set: cause 30 / secondary 21 / caption 18 / prompt 20.
- Card at y 120 / 160 / 194.
- Caption at (24,24). Pause stays. The Use button relabels to RETRY. 'TAP RETRY' is centred at y 478.

looks.wolf:
DISCLOSE: he turns and runs in at about 350 px/s. His light pool travels with him and spreads over the engineer as he arrives 40-48 px away. The engineer's rim brightens from the minimum to full #82c3e6. He lies down beside them, eye on the engineer, and his light holds steady, the warmest thing on screen. No contact.

PRESS: he stops at 150 px or more and turns his head away (lookback pose with the body toward the engineer). His light narrows to his own body (radius about 40) at 70% and does not reach the engineer, who stays in the minimum rim only. The distance between them is visible as dark floor.

Off-screen: his cyan glow bleeds in from that screen edge, next to the approved edge marker, plus the line.
looks.audio:
The cause sting is cut by the duck. The ringing tone is the same hearing-safe 2.6 kHz tone, capped at -24 dBFS, as in Look A. The world falls to a low-passed bed at -30 dB.

The one world sound kept clear is WOLF's own seam and servo hum at -18 dB:
- DISCLOSE: centred and close, staying with the engineer.
- PRESS: panned to his side, 4 dB quieter, with a slight high cut.
Deaf and hard-of-hearing players get the same contrast from the light.

The caption shows throughout, even when muted.

On RETRY: the tone fades over 0.6 s, the room tone opens, 0 ms gap.
looks.reduced_motion:
No hit-stop or shake. The collapse cuts to the down pose. The fade-down is kept, as a slow monotonic luminance ramp. WOLF still walks and his light still travels with him, with no camera movement. No light pulses, flickers or breathes at any setting; the ember is a steady glow.

Photosensitivity: zero flashes. The fade-in on retry is the only upward luminance change, at 0.40 s or longer.
references: INSIDE / Limbo: fade to black with continuous sound, death without a menu (TeenTix; private reference)
A Plague Tale: Innocence: the screen 'snaps to black' and the black does the work (Remap Radio)
Signalis: death shown as the light leaving Elster's eye (Signalis wiki)
Hollow Knight: fade back from black at the last rest (Hollow Knight wiki)
Dark Souls 'YOU DIED' on black: the counterexample for timing and size (Know Your Meme)
Private reference section 7: INSIDE iOS too dark to read; the phone visibility target

looks.name: C. Letterbox
looks.idea: The death becomes a short film shot. Black bands close in, an asymmetric 2.4:1, with a heavier bottom band that sits exactly where the dialogue panel lives today. The image partly drains and the camera eases in on the engineer and WOLF. The card reads like a subtitle in the lower band, and WOLF's stage direction sits in the top band like a screenplay note.
looks.sequence:
0.00: commit, then the cause sting and hit-stop 0.06 s. No flash.
0.00-0.15: duck to -30 dB behind a low-pass. The ringing tone starts.
0.10: the caption appears in the top band as it forms.
0.00-0.45: collapse.
0.20-0.70: the bands slide in with ease-out cubic. Top 0 to 44 px, bottom 0 to 100 px.
0.30-1.20: partial drain, one direction. Saturation to 0.35, brightness x0.80.
0.40-3.00: the camera eases from zoom 1.35 to 1.50, centred between the engineer and WOLF so both stay inside the window. The world keeps running.
0.55-0.85: the cause line fades into the bottom band. The dropped line follows at 0.70.
0.90: RETRY appears at the right of the band and input is accepted.
1.40: WOLF's line fades into the top band.
SKIP PATH: RETRY at 0.90, then 0.25 s to void, then restore at 1.15. Fade-in 0.35 s with the bands retracting over the same 0.35 s. Control at about 1.50 s.
UNSKIPPED: settled by about 3.0 s. The card holds and never auto-advances.
REPEAT DEATH: bands snap in over 0.2 s, no push-in, input at 0.60 s.

looks.wolf:
The camera frames the pair, so the reaction is staged as a two-shot.

DISCLOSE: he runs in at about 350 px/s, enters the shot and lies down 40-48 px from the engineer, facing them. The push-in ends with both centred, so the composition itself says 'together'. No contact.

PRESS: he holds at 150 px or more with his head turned away. The push-in is centred on the engineer, so WOLF sits at the frame's edge, half in shadow and still in the room.

The top-band stage direction states the gesture for anyone who misses it. Off-screen: the camera does not chase him; the edge marker sits just inside the image window, plus the line.
looks.audio:
Ringing tone and duck as in Look A: 2.6 kHz, capped at -24 dBFS, 500 Hz low-pass bed, room tone never cut.

Look C adds the room's one authored music cue, on the first death of each beat only. It is a short, non-looping procedural low pad: a 3.0 s sub swell to -20 dB that resolves into the ringing tone. Repeat deaths skip it, so it never becomes a jingle.

Caption throughout. On RETRY: the tone and pad fade over 0.6 s, 0 ms gap in the room tone.
looks.reduced_motion:
No hit-stop, no shake, no camera push-in. The zoom stays at 1.35. The bands appear with a 0.25 s alpha fade instead of sliding. The collapse cuts to the down pose. WOLF still walks. The drain is kept (monotonic).

Photosensitivity: zero flashes; the band edges never flicker; all ramps are 0.25 s or longer.
references: Film letterbox and subtitle conventions; the band replaces the existing BottomBar footprint (main.tscn, 444-526)
Saving Private Ryan / Children of Men: ringing-tone subjectivity (The Cine-Files; Tropedia 'Shell-Shock Silence')
Red Dead Redemption 2: mission death screen with restart from checkpoint (SuperCheats)
Sekiro / Dark Souls: one huge word on screen; counterexample, since our card is a calm cause sentence (AV Club; Know Your Meme)
Limbo / INSIDE: music placed by hand, at most one cue per room (private reference section 8)

spec.recommendation:
Build Look A, Cold Still, with two small borrowings from Look B.

Why A:
1. It shows the cause best. The frozen, drained frame keeps the door, sentry or cloud on screen at the moment it won, so the card's one line is confirmed by the image. That is the most informative death for a short retry.
2. It stages WOLF's choice most clearly. He is the only thing moving in a stopped world, so rushing in or holding back reads as his decision without any text, and nothing looks like a rescue.
3. It is the safest on phones. Unlike Look B, it does not rely on darkness, which the research flags as the first thing that fails on phones (INSIDE on iOS).
4. It is the safest for Reduced Motion and photosensitivity. Freezing removes motion, the drain is one ramp, and the camera never moves (unlike Look C's push-in).
5. It costs the least. It needs one canvas desaturation shader, a process pause on the room's hazard nodes, a card scene of three Labels plus the case icon, the procedural ringing bus, and one new Look 2 collapse pose (two frames) plus a WOLF lie-down pose. Look C's bands collide with the touch Use button whenever the dropped and LOST lines both show.

Borrow from B:
- WOLF's cyan eye and seam light keep their colour through the drain, so the one living hue on screen belongs to him.
- Under DISCLOSE his light softly rims the engineer, so the difference between his two reactions also reads in a still frame.

Keep in all cases:
- The 0.90 s input gate and about 1.50 s to control (the README's 1.5 s decision overrides judged.recommended's 2.4 s gate).
- No flash, the caption even when muted, and a 0 ms room-tone gap.

Next steps:
1. Confirm the 1.5 s reading, and whether engineer names can exceed about 11 characters. That length drives the 2-line wrap rule.
2. Make the collapse pose in Look 2.
3. Grey-box the card in Godot and play all three causes on desktop and on a phone before calling the feel validated. So far only the rendered layout stills in death-screen/mocks/ exist; nothing has been played.

mocks.notes:
WHAT EXISTS: these are rendered stills only. Nothing has been built in Godot, played or tested on a device. Everything is under scratchpad/death-screen/. The repo was not touched.

The previous PIL layout mocks were moved to mocks/_layout-v0/. The single storyboard frames are in mocks/story/. The per-text contrast and size data is in mocks/metrics.json.

ART (Codex built-in image_gen, edit mode, no API key). There were three jobs, each with cwd death-screen/:
- job1 'collapse': session 01a1293c-1e5f-7eb2-9fdd-6ddd7c9912a8
- job2 'honest': session 01a1293f-1eab-75d3-b9cc-6494a608d2e4
- job3 'pressed': session 01a1293f-3018-7310-bce6-470f9c86eed9

All three were archived with `codex archive` (exit 0, logs in art/logs/). Jobs 2 and 3 ran in parallel, so "newest rollout with this cwd" would have been ambiguous. Instead I archived each one by the session id printed in its own output, after checking that the rollout's cwd was death-screen/.

The selected outputs are art/collapse.png, art/honest.png and art/pressed.png (1672x941). Raw attempts are in art/raw/. Prompts and reference roles are in art/jobs/ and art/notes.md.

Codex rejected all three of its job1 attempts on guide-box bounds. I chose raw a204d2af myself: curled pose, face hidden, no blood. A finer mask then showed the engineer is about 1.6x game scale (about 271 px long, not 165). So the compositor cuts the actors out by difference mask (tools/prep_scene.py), scales the engineer by 0.60 and WOLF by 0.88, and re-places them at true game scale on the plate. Codex's own verdict on honest.png was "closest of three", with WOLF's head a bit high. The pose reads correctly after re-placement.

The WOLF cut-outs carry some filled dark plate between the legs. This is invisible at game scale.

COMPOSITION: Chrome 154 canvas through the Playwright bundled with the ChatGPT app (tools/compose.mjs drives tools/compose.js). Both WOFF2 fonts loaded through FontFace (the font check returned true for each).
- World layers: the Look 2 plate at the real desktop camera (zoom 1.35, deck at 70% of the frame) and the touch camera (deck at 62%).
- Hazards: the HQ sentry-active cut-out, and the junction blast door layers (armed and breaking at the hit, frame-off plus blown debris after). The corridor plate stands in for the junction.
- Smoke and frost: procedural soft blobs, not painted.
- Look treatments are per-pixel, applied to separate world, actor and front layers:
  - A: world goes to saturation 0.08 and brightness x0.62 with a cold multiply, capped at L* 70. Actors go to 0.30 and x0.80.
  - B: world exposure drops to 4%. WOLF keeps his cyan seam light. His light pool covers the engineer on the honest route and stays on his own body on the pressed route. The engineer gets a minimum #4175a0 rim at 60%. One steady 25% ember marks the cause: the sentry's red eye, the door's amber lamps, or the frost.
  - C: bars close and the world goes to saturation 0.35 and brightness x0.80.
- No flashes in any frame.

The spec text I received was cut off partway through Look B, so Look C's details are rebuilt from the earlier mock.py ('Letterbox': top bar 48 and bottom bar 100 canvas px, cause line set in the bottom bar). Treat Look C as provisional.

The storyboard is blast on the honest route: HIT 0.00 s, COLLAPSE 0.45 s, DRAIN 0.75 s, CARD from 0.90 s. WOLF appears at his end pose from frame 3 because there is no in-between art. The HUD is not drawn in the hit frame.

The phone frame is a generic 19.5:9 phone at 2340x1080, density 2.75. The 960x540 canvas is pillarboxed to 1920x1080 at x 210, with a punch-hole in the left pillarbox and a faint dashed 24 dp (66 px) gesture-inset guide.

Phone layout:
- Pause stays on screen.
- The Use button (773,345)-(928,435) is relabelled RETRY. That is 310x180 px, about 113x65 dp, well over 48 dp.
- TAP RETRY sits at y 478.
- Every text bottom is at or above canvas y 507.
- Look C on the phone moves the caption chip just under the top bar so it doesn't collide with the WOLF line.

TEXT SIZES (canvas px -> device px):
- Desktop 1280x720 (x1.333):
  - Cause line: 26 -> 34.7 (Look C: 24 -> 32)
  - Dropped and WOLF lines: 18 -> 24 (Look C WOLF line: 17 -> 22.7)
  - Caption: 16 -> 21.3
  - RETRY prompt and keycap: 18 -> 24
  - The smallest text, 16 canvas px, is 32 px at 1080p, which clears the Xbox XAG 18 px and 26 px minimums.
- Phone (x2, then /2.75 for dp):
  - Cause: 30 -> 60 px (21.8 dp); Look C 28 -> 56
  - Dropped and WOLF lines: 21 -> 42 px (15.3 dp)
  - Caption: 18 -> 36 px (13.1 dp)
  - TAP RETRY: 20 -> 40 px (14.5 dp)
  - Pause label 17 and RETRY button 23 canvas px
- No line wraps with "Rowan".

CONTRAST (WCAG ratio of text colour to the background under each line's bounding box, measured on the actual frame before the text was drawn; reported as the 95th-percentile background pixel and the brightest pixel):
- Every text element passes 4.5:1, even against the single brightest pixel.
- Lowest p95: 8.75:1, Look A phone TAP RETRY, which sits over the lamp's floor reflection.
- Lowest brightest-pixel: 6.99:1, Look A phone WOLF line.
- Look A desktop: cause 16.4, dropped 13.8, WOLF 9.7, caption 10.7, RETRY 16.5, keycap glyph 9.2.
- Look B (void): everything 10.5 to 18.7.
- Look C (bars): everything 10.7 to 18.6.
- One fix came from this: Look A's keycap glyph first measured 4.12 (3.51 at the brightest pixel) over the floor reflection. A 72% dark keycap fill raised it to 9.17.

DESIGN READ:
- At the true game camera the collapsed engineer is only about 126x34 px at 1280. A and C read clearly. In B the engineer survives only as the rim plus WOLF's light, so B needs a phone brightness check.
- Coolant in Look B gives WOLF a slightly teal cast where his light hits the frost.
